links.comparator_used: Eye care professional (ECP) referral/exam for diabetic eye screening, with patient choice between AI and ECP under copay manipulation
links.outcome: Patient choice of autonomous AI vs ECP screening (uptake), perceived AI effectiveness, and desire for second-opinion reconfirmation
links.effect: AI selected by 81% with no copay vs 43% with $50 copay (p < 0.001); perceived AI effectiveness 3.67 vs 3.24 (p = 0.02); incentive source (insurer vs AI developer) did not affect choice
links.tradeoff: Patients choosing AI (vs ECP) were far more likely to seek human reconfirmation after abnormal (mean 6.69 vs 2.41) or normal (3.43 vs 2.47) results (both p < 0.001), so AI uptake did not remove demand for ECP exams.
links.quote: Waiving the copay significantly increased AI selection (81% vs. 43%, p < 0.001); the source of the incentive did not affect choice.

design_hint: copay waiver incentive for AI screening and human reconfirmation
